title: Jordyn's first car
subtitle: Safety first, then cost to own · under $15k · 130 mi/week
intro: Every car we can find under $15k that could work as Jordyn's first car, grouped by whether automatic emergency braking is actually standard for that model year — not just theoretically available. Within each group they're ranked on total cost to own, not sticker price: fuel or charging, teen-driver insurance, maintenance, Washington's EV fee, depreciation, and a battery allowance for the electrics. Electric and plug-in cars get no bonus here; where they win, they win on cost. Switch between the 2-year (Jordyn) and 6-year (through Emma) windows to see which cars still make sense long-term. Tap 👍/👎 and add notes, then hit "Send my picks."

niceToHaves: Backup camera (all of these have one)
avoid: Badly degraded EV battery (esp. air-cooled Leaf)

guide.note: Safety features vary a LOT by year, trim, and optioned packages on these cars — AEB and blind-spot are often trim- or package-dependent, so ALWAYS confirm them per-VIN before you fall in love. Ranges are EPA estimates; real-world winter range on an EV runs ~20–30% lower.
